extracted.intended_audience: researchers in symplectic topology / symplectic geometers familiar with pseudo-holomorphic curves and ECH
extracted.subtask_description: Corrected existence and construction conditions for finite-energy J-holomorphic planes/cylinders in symplectic cobordisms (mainly CP^2 minus an ellipsoid), including index, asymptotic, regularity, and gluing requirements used to obtain obstructions to symplectic embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original existence theorem (Theorem 2.36 / Theorem 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed natural d and irrational S > sqrt(3d), with E = E(1/S,1) and (CP^2 \ E)^{-}_infty the negative symplectic completion of CP^2(R) \ E, there exist an admissible almost complex structure J and a regular finite energy J-holomorphic plane of degree d in (CP^2 \ E)^{-}_infty whose negative end is asymptotic to the (3d-1)-fold cover of the simple closed Reeb orbit on E with period π/S^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires R>1 so E can be identified in CP^2(R); S must be irrational and satisfy S>sqrt(3d); 'admissible' J and regular finite energy plane are as in symplectic field theory setup. (This is the original statement that contained the proof error noted below.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of the error: embeddedness assumption overlooked
rubrics_metrics.description: The original proof inadvertently implied the constructed curves were embedded, which contradicts results of Hutchings and Taubes because the ECH partition conditions and writhe inequality force the writhe inequality to be an equality, conflicting with embeddedness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The error arose in the proof of Lemma 2.53 of the original paper where the possibility that the curves G^ε are multiply covered was not accounted for. One must therefore allow for multiply-covered curves in the compactness/degeneration analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected existence theorem (Theorem 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The conclusions of Theorem 1 hold provided d = g_{n+1} for some n, where {g_n}_{n >= 1} are the odd-index Fibonacci numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This weaker/existence-for-a-sequence result suffices for the original application since the proof only needs curves for a sequence d → ∞. The paper proves existence for those specific degrees by assembling cylinders and planes and gluing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation and scaling conventions for ellipsoids and CP^2
rubrics_metrics.description: Ellipsoid notation: ℰ(a_1,...,a_n) = { π|z_1|^2/a_1 + ... + π|z_n|^2/a_n ≤ 1 } = E( sqrt(a_1/π), ..., sqrt(a_n/π) ). Scaled ellipsoid c ℰ(a_1,...,a_n). CP^2(A) denotes CP^2 scaled so lines have area A. For ℰ(a,b) assume a < b and a/b irrational so boundary has exactly two simple closed Reeb orbits denoted α (faster) and β (slower) with periods a and b respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conventions determine the contact forms, Reeb orbits, and quantitative data (periods) used throughout; correct normalization is required for index computations and embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conley–Zehnder index formulas for iterates on irrational ellipsoids
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These explicit formulas are used to match indices of asymptotic orbits in gluing and to verify index-equality conditions (e.g., Eq. (3) equating CZ of α_1^{(3g_{n+1}-1)} and α_2^{(g_{n+2})}). Correct computation is essential to ensure index zero objects and to exclude negative-index multiple covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of index-zero J-holomorphic cylinder connecting specified covers (Proposition 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For generic admissible J on X_1^2 (the completion of ℰ_2 \ int(ℰ_1)) and all sufficiently small ε>0, there is a regular J-holomorphic cylinder u : R×S^1 → X_1^2 of index zero whose negative end is asymptotic to α_1^{(3g_{n+1}-1)} and whose positive end is asymptotic to α_2^{(g_{n+2})}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from Theorem 2 of [7] after verifying the CZ indices agree (Eq. (3)). Genericity of J is required for regularity; ε smallness and choices of c_1 ensure containment relations of ellipsoids used to form X_1^2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of an index-zero J-holomorphic building (Pardon's consequence) (Proposition 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any admissible J on X_1^2 there exists a cylindrical J-holomorphic building of index zero with one negative end asymptotic to α_1^{(3g_{n+1}-1)} and one positive end asymptotic to α_2^{(g_{n+2})}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This existence result is an immediate consequence of Pardon's invariance of contact homology and the odd CZ indices on irrational ellipsoids; it provides the broken object from which the desired cylinder is extracted by further index and covering arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dichotomy for curves in symplectization levels (Lemma 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a curve v of the building maps to Y_1 or Y_2 (the symplectizations of boundary ellipsoids), then either the index of v is positive, or v has index zero and covers a trivial cylinder over a closed Reeb orbit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This alternative (proved using index formulas, floor-function inequalities, and Stokes' theorem) is used to show all nontrivial pieces in symplectization levels must be trivial cylinders for index reasons, leaving a unique nontrivial curve in the cobordism level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonnegativity of indices for curves in the cobordism level under genericity (Lemma 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If J is generic so that every somewhere injective genus-zero J-holomorphic curve is regular, then each curve u of the building with image in X_1^2 has nonnegative index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The condition S > 3g_{n+1} - 1 is used to bound growth of CZ indices of covers of α_1 and thereby exclude multiple covers with negative index; combined with genericity this ensures no negative-index curves remain in the cobordism level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity and immersion consequences for somewhere injective index-zero cylinders
rubrics_metrics.description: For generic J, the cylinder u covers a regular, somewhere injective J-holomorphic cylinder v of index zero. Corollary 3.17 of [18] implies v is immersed; since u and v are cylinders this implies u has no critical points and regularity follows from Theorem 1 of [18].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus regularity is achieved by: (i) generic choice of J making somewhere-injective genus-0 curves regular, (ii) obtaining an immersed somewhere-injective representative, (iii) ruling out critical points for cylinder covers, and (iv) applying analytic results to conclude regularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of embedded genus-0 degree g_{n+1} plane in the complementary cobordism (Proposition 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an admissible J on X_2^3 (completion of CP^2(...) \ Φ(int ℰ_2)), if ε is sufficiently small and c_2 is sufficiently close to 1, there exists a connected, embedded (hence regular) J-holomorphic plane v of genus 0, degree g_{n+1} with negative end asymptotic to α_2^{(g_{n+2})}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposition is proved in [3] using ECH-to-ECH isomorphisms defined via Seiberg–Witten theory and the foundational work of Hutchings–Taubes. Small ε and c_2 ≈ 1 ensure the embedding/compactness hypotheses hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly via gluing: producing the final plane
rubrics_metrics.description: Given regular u (cylinder in X_1^2) and regular v (plane in X_2^3) whose asymptotic orbits match, the standard gluing procedure produces a regular pseudo-holomorphic plane in (CP^2(A) \ int(ℰ_1))^{-}_infty of degree g_{n+1} whose negative end is asymptotic to α_1^{(3g_{n+1}-1)}; rescaling replaces ℰ_1 by E(1/√S,1) and CP^2(A) by CP^2(√(A/S)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gluing requires matching asymptotic covers, regularity of the pieces, and stretching the neck along the contact hypersurface; standard SFT gluing theorems apply. The final rescaling step adjusts to the normalization used in the statement of Theorem 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of arithmetic properties of Fibonacci indices and coprimeness remark
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a sequence n_k → ∞ such that gcd(3g_{n_k+1}-1, g_{n_k+2}) = 1, so for such n_k the corresponding cylinder u is somewhere injective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This number-theoretic observation (avoiding divisibility by 2 or 5) is used to guarantee somewhere-injectivity in infinitely many degrees, strengthening the existence results in particular cases and aiding immersion/regularity arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative route / full restoration (McDuff remark)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recent preprint of McDuff (see Lemma 2.6 of [15]) shows Theorem 1 (the original stronger statement) is in fact true as stated: combining the cylinder construction with obstruction-bundle gluing produces planes for all d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates that by using obstruction-bundle gluing one can overcome the multiply-covered curve issue in the original argument and obtain the stronger full-existence statement; practitioners may consult [15] for that approach.
